decision: TEAM DECISION, taken under Joshua's 2026-09-05 delegation ('work with the team to make the call - this doesn't seem like a me thing'). CHOICE: option (b) -- human-gated swap via the 6hrv kickstart, verify the process is alive AND reporting the new build_id, and keep the drift denominator honest until it is. NOT (a): accepting 1/4 MISMATCH permanently makes a MISMATCH that can never clear, and AGENTS.md already records why that is corrosive -- 'a MISMATCH that can never clear is not a gate; it is noise that trains operators to ignore the gate', measured on pane-truth installed-from-elsewhere. NOT (c): repointing ai.zeststream.omp-orchestrator.control-plane at THIS repo is a cross-repo ownership change, materially larger than an install, and it would ride along inside an install lane where nobody would review it as the ownership transfer it is. EVIDENCE FOR (b): bead omp-orchestrator-2tny records the live hazard in its own words -- 'the live supervisor binary was unlinked while running: every liveness surface reported healthy, only ls told the truth' -- so an unguarded replace of a binary under launchd KeepAlive=True is exactly the failure this repo has already paid for once. Pane 4 independently deferred it as human-gated and installed the other three (3/4 IDENTITY OK, 1/4 MISMATCH, verified independently by pane 1), which is the correct conservative split. BINDING CONDITIONS on execution: (1) the swap is gated, not automatic -- an agent may not replace ~/.local/bin/omp-orchestrator as a side effect of any other lane; (2) postconditions are BOTH liveness and identity -- the process must be alive after the kickstart AND report the new build_id, because 2tny proves liveness alone is not evidence; (3) if either postcondition fails, restore the prior artifact and report, since AGENTS.md requires rollback to restore bytes and never recompile through a broken lane; (4) the drift denominator stays at 4 and the MISMATCH stays visible until identity actually clears -- do not shrink the denominator to manufacture a clean ratio. RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden: the loaded launchd unit still serves the control-plane repo, so even a successful swap leaves a cross-repo ownership question open. That question is deliberately NOT decided here and remains available for Joshua; (b) makes the binary honest without pre-empting it.

decision: TEAM DECISION, taken under Joshua's 2026-09-05 delegation. CHOICE: schedule fleet-monitor ONLY, and only with its own --state path; reap-finished-panes and refill-idle-panes are NOT scheduled. REASONS, each measured. (1) All three are one-shot sweeps rather than daemons -- pane 4's own INSTALLED=5/5 RUNNING=0/5 census established that, with NEEDS_CALLER_NOT_PROCESS naming dispatch-silence-watch, bead-availability, reap-finished-panes, refill-idle-panes and fleet-monitor. A one-shot sweep needs a CALLER; putting a sweep on a timer is not the same as giving it a caller, and only fleet-monitor is genuinely periodic (one attention tick, and it is the only scheduled writer of the standing admission verdict). (2) refill-idle-panes --apply STAYS REFUSED regardless of any schedule, under Joshua's 2026-09-03 no-auto-refill ruling recorded in CONTRACT.md Wave 3 and HD-0015: 'we dont want to automatically refill panes with work without being approved'. Its --plan lane is a proposal and already emits APPROVAL_REQUIRED detector=actuation-withheld; scheduling a proposal nobody reads would reproduce the exact defect this session measured twice. (3) THE OVERLAP TRAP IS MEASURED, NOT THEORETICAL: pane 4 reported OVERLAP_VERDICT=overlaps:tick-monitor-observe-vs-fleet-monitor-admission-verdict, and this session independently produced LEDGER CONTENDED when two watchers shared the default tick-monitor ledger -- one watcher's last_tick advanced on the wrong cadence and silently disabled the two-capture liveness rule, reporting gap_secs_too_short as no error. So a scheduled fleet-monitor MUST carry --state pointing at a path no other watcher owns, and that condition is part of this decision rather than an implementation detail. (4) EVERY SCHEDULED MONITOR NEEDS A NAMED READER: tick-monitor ran 101 consecutive ticks reporting free_capacity_streak=101 with verdict=None and nobody read it; ATTENTION.txt took 178 writes with zero readers. A schedule without a reader manufactures a file that grows. fleet-monitor's reader is the standing admission verdict that controller-tick consumes, which is why it is the one that qualifies. NOT DECIDED HERE and left open: the schedule INTERVAL. Joshua's own measured discipline applies -- this session derived a wake bound from observed completion times (median 10 min, max 16, bound = max + 50%) rather than picking a round number, and the same method should set this interval from observed attention-tick need rather than a guess. Until that measurement exists the interval is UNKNOWN, and an unmeasured interval is not a schedule.
question: Should fleet-monitor, reap-finished-panes, and refill-idle-panes --plan be put on a schedule in THIS repo, and if so what schedule? Options: (i) no schedule -- the conductor invokes them on demand during reap, which is the current de facto state and keeps a human in every loop; (ii) schedule reap-finished-panes and refill --plan only, leaving fleet-monitor manual to avoid the ledger overlap; (iii) schedule all three with distinct state paths and a declared reader for each.
